sources.title: AWS Certified Developer - Associate: Exam Guide (DVA-C03)
sources.note: Domains, weights, task statements, skills, response types, scoring and service lists transcribed from the official PDF (read pages 1-20; PDF metadata creation date 2026-10-30). The `scope` arrays are CONDENSED from the guide's skill statements (names and concepts only).

sources.title: AWS Certified Developer - Associate (certification page)
sources.note: Source of the 130-minute duration, 65-question total and 150 USD price. These figures are NOT in the DVA-C03 guide itself; confirm the time limit for DVA-C03 when registration opens.

version.note: Per the guide: 'Registration for the updated version of the exam (DVA-C03) opens December 1, 2026. The last day to take the current version of the exam (DVA-C02) is November 30, 2026.' DVA-C02 (guide Version 1.3) had weights 32/26/24/18 and a different task structure; this pack is for DVA-C03 only.

exam.name: AWS Certified Developer - Associate
exam.passMarkNote: Official pass mark is a scaled score of 720 on a 100-1000 scale (compensatory scoring: only the overall result matters). The raw-percentage equivalent is not published, so 72% is a PROXY for display on mock results only.
exam.readinessTargetNote: Your own per-exam target for dashboard/map status (default 80%). Not a vendor figure.
exam.timeLimitNote: From the AWS certification page, not the exam guide. Verify for DVA-C03.
exam.unscoredNote: 15 unscored questions are not identified on the real exam. Unanswered = incorrect; no penalty for guessing. Multiple response requires ALL correct options to earn credit.

questionTypes.single: Multiple choice: 1 correct response, 3 distractors (4 options).
questionTypes.multi: Multiple response: 2 or more correct responses out of 5 or more options; all correct options must be selected for credit.

objectives.title: Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS.
scope: Tightly vs loosely coupled systems; decoupling components with AWS services
Synchronous vs asynchronous patterns (API Gateway invocation, SQS processing, EventBridge workflows)
Fault-tolerant, resilient applications (retry with backoff, graceful degradation)
Creating/extending/maintaining APIs (request/response transformations, validation rules)
Code that uses AWS APIs and SDKs; streaming data; serialization/deserialization
Event-driven patterns (EventBridge, S3 Event Notifications, SQS, SNS)
AI-assisted development tools (generate, review, optimize code; spec-driven generation, automated reviews, completion, refactoring, security scanning)
Integrating managed AWS AI services into applications

objectives.title: Develop code for AWS Lambda.
scope: Lambda access to private resources in VPCs
Configuration: environment variables, memory, concurrency, timeout, runtime, handler, layers, extensions
Event lifecycles and errors (Lambda destinations, dead-letter queues)
Integrations via code, event source mappings, destinations (API Gateway, DynamoDB)

objectives.title: Use data stores during application development.
scope: Data lifecycles (S3 Lifecycle policies, TTL, retention periods)
Choosing data stores by access pattern (ElastiCache, DynamoDB, S3, RDS)
Caching solution based on data store
DynamoDB: high-cardinality partition keys, read consistency models, query vs scan, keys/attributes/indexes

objectives.title: Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services.
scope: Identity federation
Access control (fine-grained permissions, security tokens, MFA)
Programmatic access; authenticated calls to AWS services
Presigned URLs for secure, time-limited access (S3, CloudFront)
Permissions for IAM principals (users, roles, services) and resources
Assuming an IAM role

objectives.title: Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services.
scope: Encryption at rest and in transit
Certificates (AWS Certificate Manager, AWS Private CA)
Client-side vs server-side encryption; using encryption keys
Generating certificates and SSH keys for development
Identify, mask and limit access to sensitive data (PII, PHI)
Secret management services

objectives.title: Identify and mitigate security risks associated with using and integrating AI services into application development.
scope: Requesting and managing access to AI services
Data privacy controls (VPC endpoints for private connectivity; inputs/outputs not used to train models)
Filtering/controlling model inputs and outputs (content filtering, sensitive information detection, PII/PHI redaction, denied topics, prompt injection protection)
Securing AI agent interactions (tool-use authorization, session isolation, human-in-the-loop approvals)
Protecting sensitive content in monitoring logs

objectives.title: Prepare application artifacts to be deployed to AWS.
scope: Dependencies for code modules within packages
Container images (Amazon ECR, Dockerfiles, image tagging, lifecycle policies)
Code repositories in deployment environments
Environment-specific configuration (AWS AppConfig, Systems Manager Parameter Store, Secrets Manager, API Gateway, Lambda)
API Gateway features and resources (stage-specific URLs, endpoints)

objectives.title: Implement and automate application testing in AWS environments.
scope: Developing and validating tests (AWS SAM, AWS CDK, CloudFormation)
Mock APIs for external dependencies (API Gateway)
Application test events (JSON payloads for Lambda and API Gateway)
Application environments (Lambda aliases, container image tags, Amplify branches, Copilot environments, API Gateway APIs)
AWS AI tools to generate tests and automate repetitive testing workflows

objectives.title: Deploy code by using AWS continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) services.
scope: Lambda packaging (.zip, container images, layers)
Containerized deployments (ECS task definitions, EKS manifests, Fargate launch types, rolling updates)
Infrastructure as code (CloudFormation, SAM templates)
AWS CodeDeploy; AWS CodePipeline orchestration
Deployment strategies (blue/green, canary, rolling)
Automatic or manual rollback (CloudFormation, CodeDeploy)
Source control for versions and releases (labels, branches)
AWS AI tools in CI/CD workflows

objectives.title: Assist in a root cause analysis.
scope: Debugging code and service integration issues
Interpreting application metrics, logs and traces
Querying logs
Troubleshooting deployment failures from output logs
AWS AI tools to analyze errors and suggest fixes

objectives.title: Apply logging, monitoring, and observability best practices.
scope: Effective logging strategies (structured logging)
Code that emits custom metrics
Notification alerts (quota limits, deployment completions)
Tracing with AWS services and tools
Workload health (application health checks, liveness and readiness probes)

objectives.title: Optimize applications by using AWS services and features.
scope: Concurrency (Lambda provisioned concurrency, EC2 Auto Scaling, thread pool management, connection pooling)
Optimizing memory and compute power
Messaging optimization (SQS queues, SNS fan-out)
Caching (ElastiCache, DynamoDB Accelerator, CloudFront)
Detecting performance bottlenecks (CloudWatch)
AWS AI tools to find optimization opportunities
